frames.text: Within forty-eight hours of learning something new, your brain will silently erase nearly seventy percent of it. Why is human memory so fragile?
In eighteen eighty-five, German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus conducted the first rigorous scientific study of memory, discovering the mathematical Forgetting Curve.
Memory decays exponentially over time. But if you actively retrieve the information just before you forget it, the decay curve instantly resets and flattens.
Passive re-reading tricks your brain into a false illusion of mastery. Spaced retrieval creates desirable difficulty, forcing the brain to reinforce long-term structural storage.
Forgetting is not a flaw in your biology. It is an intelligent filtering algorithm. Active recall is how you signal what is too important to delete.
Stop cramming in single marathon sessions. Space out your reviews, test your recall, and lock knowledge into permanent memory.
